headline: Ethan Hawke returns for The Lowdown season 2
post:
Ethan Hawke is back as Tulsa truthstorian Lee Raybon in the season two premiere of The Lowdown on FX and Hulu. According to The Hollywood Reporter, the new episodes hit the ground running with plenty of fresh problems and a brand new case. Lee kicks things off by taking a mushroom gummy before a journalism speech and calling everyone in the room sellouts and losers. That chaotic moment brings him into contact with a public defender named Ginger, played by Betty Gilpin, who pulls him into a missing prisoner mystery involving a vanished inmate named Mekko Dean.

Meanwhile, Lee's estranged father, played by Tommy Lee Jones, arrives in town after being picked up by a police officer on a country road. While initially appearing confused in an ill-fitting suit and a cap referencing Psalms 107:29, Tommy Lee Jones and Ethan Hawke shared in an interview that the father is actually trying to score a free ride to his son's doorstep.

Creator Sterlin Harjo explained that this round leans even further into comedy because the world was already established in the first season. Are you watching the new season? 📺

#TheLowdown #EthanHawke #FX
original_title: ‘The Lowdown’ Brings a New Case and New Problems for Ethan Hawke’s Lee in Season 2 Premiere

headline: Walmart item compares to Rhode Glazing Milk
post:
Hey friends! Have you heard about the viral budget-friendly skincare find making waves online? According to E! News, shoppers have pointed out that the Vitamasques Hydrate Milk Glaze Moisturizer sold at Walmart might be an affordable alternative to the popular Rhode Glazing Milk.

After looking closely at the ingredients, researchers found that both items share 12 components. They both offer deep hydration, a plumping effect, and a nice glass-skin finish. However, the $10 Vitamasques option contains peptides for firming, while Rhode uses more lipid-rich ceramides to support the skin barrier.

Happy reviewers shared that they love the dewy results, and some even called it a "Great dupe of luxury brand". Would you try this budget-friendly alternative?
